main_text.p: {a}iubilare, ... Nicia Athenienses, pacem in Lacones, sed quae sexdecim diuturnitatem annos & decem menses duravit, constitutam. Alterum periodus ... constat.
Primo Corinthiorum cum Argivis, Mantinenses & Eleos ex Isthmo ... Spartani, Ampelo ... Pylus, obvenit.
Pharsalia Lacedaemonum cum Boeotis, Atheniensium cum Argivis, Mantineis & Eleis foedera incidunt.

Pars Argivorum in Epidaurios bellum movent, quam illis Atheniensibus, his, Spartanis suppetias ferentibus, ad ultimum usque huius periodi annum, decimo fere, Argivorum fortuna magis Atheniensium & Spartanorum damnum gestum est.
Tertia Periodus ad obitum Darii II. existit.

In ea primum multa in Thraciam, Euboeam, Lesbiorum, Chiorum, & Erythraeorum defectiones, Thucyd. I. 8. Abydi a Pericylide Spartano: demptis ... quaedam ... in Olympiam ... Thrasyllo & Thrasylo ad Abydum ...
Spartanis victoriam, occisum ad Cyzicum ... Achaeorum & Pitharum, ... urbes in Thracia recepsit, ... Pylum revocatum, quae ... Herrae dejectus ... pollutus.
Alcibiadem, victoriam ... Lydiam ... Caeciliam ... Atheniensium ... Hinc Athenae obsidens, & fame ... ad muros ... disciplinam ... Neque excepta ... Lacedaemonem, Miletum ... Atheniensem.
In Thraciam praesul Chiorum ... Thucyd. ... Spartano nepos, quem excepit ... Amor.

page.notes: Much of the text is very faint and worn, especially along the left margin and the lower half; many words are not legible and the transcription of those lines is approximate or uncertain. Marginal line numbers at the left (e.g. 5, 10, 15 ...) and references to Thucydides (Thucyd. I. 5, I. 6, I. 8) appear in the margins; the exact placement of the small marginal numbers and references could not be fully read. Parts of the Greek-letter and Latin marginal notes are illegible.
